text: DERBY WINNER'S NEW PURCHASE

label: text
text: MARE'S RECORD PRICE.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Reuter's Service.)

label: text
text: A record price of 17,000 guineas for a brood mare was paid on behalf of H. H. the Aga Khan for Straitlace, the winner of last year's Oaks, at the sale of the late Sir Edward Hulton's horses.

label: text
text: The second highest price on the first day was 12,500 guineas, paid by Mr. H. E. Morriss of Shanghai, for Soubriquet.

label: text
text: Mr. Solly Joel paid 13,500 guineas for Oojah which was struck out from the Derby owing to the owner's death.

label: text
text: The total of the first two days sale exceeded 242,000 guineas.

label: text
text: It transpires that Mr. Esmond, not the Aga Khan, was the purchaser of Straitlace which goes to France where Mr. Esmond will train and breed extensively.

label: text
text: [Mr. H. E. Morriss of Shanghai won the 2,000 Guineas and the Derby with Manna and he also has a two-year-old.]

label: text
text: LATEST RESULTS

label: text
text: Of the latest county cricket results to hand the most interesting is the defeat of Laicashire by Surrey, the Oval team taking ample revenge for humiliation earlier in the season.

label: text
text: Yorkshire continue their all-conquering career, their latest victims being Kent.

label: text
text: There were no abnormal scores but Howell, the former Test Match fast bowler who was one of the M.C.C. team in Australia last close season but not picked for any of the Tests, took nine wickets in one innings. He has a still better feat to his credit as in 1923 he took all ten of Yorkshire's wickets at Edgbaston.

label: doc_title
text: THE TYPHOON

label: text
text: The typhoon was first indicated on the weather map on the afternoon of July 9, when it was situated between Yap and Guam. It moved on a W.N.W. course and crossed or passed N. Luzon in the immediate vicinity of Aparri in the early hours of July 13.

label: text
text: It then pursued a N.N.W. track until the morning of the 14th, when observations received indicated that it was situated to the north of the Pescadores. There were several apparent discrepancies in the observations from Formosa and as by the afternoon of the 14th the centre appeared to be near Swatow, it was concluded that the position given in the morning was in error.

label: text
text: The typhoon actually passed north of the Pescadores however and then maintained a W.S.W. track entering the coast near Swatow. It is now situated to the north of Canton in the form of a depression, filling up.

label: text
text: The track of the typhoon was unusual; but similar instances are on record. The actual movement of the barometer on account of the typhoon was masked to a considerable degree by extensive superposed fluctuations caused by the thunderstorms of yesterday afternoon.

label: paragraph_title
text: LUCKY ESCAPE.

label: text
text: ALARMING STUBBS ROAD ACCIDENT.

label: text
text: CAR STRIKES PARAPET.

label: text
text: Mr. H. S. Bennett, manager of the Hongkong Telephone Co., and two friends had a lucky escape from serious injury on Monday afternoon. They were proceeding to the Peak by Stubbs Road when their car met with a nasty mishap. They were approaching the second bend after the hairpin bend when a tyre burst and the car ran into the granite wall at the cliff side. Mr. Bennett was flung violently against the wind-screen but luckily escaped with nothing more serious than a few scratches and bruises. His two friends were thrown from the car by the force of the impact, also fortunately without serious injury. That all three escaped so lightly, when they might easily have been involved in the gravest consequences, was largely due to the fact that the car was travelling at not more than 15 miles an hour.

label: text
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: New York, July 14.

label: text
text: The Standard Oil Company of New Jersey has announced the adoption of an eight-hour day in its mid-continental oilfields, also a new wages scale which will partly compensate workers for the resultant loss in wages.

label: paragraph_title
text: RUBBER

label: text
text: RISE MERELY TEMPORARY.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: London, July 14.

label: text
text: The rubber restriction policy was again the subject of questions in the House of Commons when the Hon. W. G. Ormsby-Gore, replying, said that according to the best estimates of the situation and prospects of the plantation rubber industry, he could only regard the extent of the present rise as a temporary movement. There appeared no ground at present for special enquiry or for proposing that the Ceylon and Malaya Governments should repeal their existing legislative measures. If there was a prospect that there would be a real shortage in the course of next few months, it would be possible to release the maximum production. There was no reason why growers should not increase production in anticipation of a shortage. He was aware that, since the introduction of the restriction scheme, Dutch plantation rubber had increased by from 15 to 37 per cent. and that bulk rubber, in which the middlemen were gambling at four shillings per lb., was sold by the producer between 1/5. and 1/10 per lb.

label: text
text: Mr. Waddington asked if the Government was aware that producers were accumulating stocks with a view to the termination of the Stevenson export restrictions in February, and asked if it was not in the trade interests to permit more exports now to prevent a slump in February?

label: text
text: Mr. Ormsby-Gore considered this too long as a supplementary question. He added that he made a slip in reply yesterday. The whole matter was being watched with the advice of an expert committee, and while they agreed that the price was likely to fall considerably, they did not think that the abolition or modification of the Stevenson scheme would materially assist either now or in a few months.

label: text
text: Replying to a suggestion from Mr. Thomas, Mr. Ormsby-Gore said that he would consider the advisability of an immediate statement with regard to the future.

label: text
text: WARSHIP ASSIST.

label: paragraph_title
text: (Router's Service.)

label: text
text: A message from Port Sudan says that from a telegram from Massowah, it appears that the Italian-motor-vessel-Esquilino, from Trieste to Shanghai, is ashore on a reef.

label: text
text: An Italian warship and eighteen dhows (small junks) have left Massowah to assist.

label: text
text: [The Esquilino was out on her first trip to the Far East. Messrs. Dodwell & Co., Ltd., the local agents, informed the “China Mail” that the vessel was due here; in ordinary events, in August. There may have been a few Italian passengers for Hongkong, but particulars are not available.]

label: text
text: Melbourne, July 13.—Lord Strudbroke, on behalf of Victoria, has sent a wireless message to Admiral Coontz, saying "Heartiest welcome to the officers and men of the great American Fleet now approaching our shores." The Parliament of Victoria will adjourn during the visit of the U.S. fleet.—Reuter,

label: paragraph_title
text: OBITUARY:

label: text
text:
The deaths of two members of the Portuguese community took place at Kowloon yesterday.
Mr. Hernnegildo Maria Basto passed away at his residence No. 94, Nathan Road at 6.15 p.m., at the age of 73. The deceased gentleman was a share and estate broker, and, besides other relatives who will be known as Mr. J. M. C. Basto (brother) and Messrs. C. H. and A. H. Basto (nephews). The funeral will pass the Monument at 5.15 p.m. to-day.
Mr. Charles Osmund passed away at a ripe old age at his residence, No. 1, Liberty Avenue, at 12.45 a.m. The funeral will pass the Monument at 4.30 p.m. to-day.

label: text
text: The return of the Maharashtra and the young Maharashtra of Gwalior and suite to India is not yet fixed, but it is stated that it will be fixed as soon as possible. They are at present staying in a hotel at Neuilly, where the Maharashtra died. The ashes of the Maharashtra will be left at the cemetery of Pere La Chaise until the departure of the party to India.
